rubric_items.reason: All four acceptance criteria (ticket L16-L20) map to REQ-1, REQ-2, REQ-4, REQ-5; the open timing value is listed under Out of scope with a reason.
Most REQs are atomic. REQ-2 says the same condition twice (24h and 'within one day'), REQ-10 leaves the state after rescheduling open, and REQ-14 is a process action, not system behaviour.

Most known items cite IDE answers correctly, but REQ-10 (reschedule) is marked known on A-03, which only says staff can 'close' a Stale appointment. The summary's 'first background job' claim has no cite.
The clash with glossary#scheduled and intent-baseline#closed-appointments was asked as Q-03 citing both, answered in A-03, and recorded as a mismatch.
The questions are precise, offer real options and a proposed default, and the glossary question was marked non-blocking.
Plain and consistent glossary terms. Backtick quoting in statements is uneven, for example 'within one day' inside REQ-2.

findings.text: REQ-10 (staff can reschedule a Stale appointment) is marked known on A-03, but A-03's answer only says staff can 'close' it. The glossary treats move and close as separate actions, so reschedule goes beyond the user's answer.

cites.quote: Staff can still reschedule (`move`) a Stale appointment.
answer: Staff can still close it (proposed default)

findings.suggested_fix: Mark REQ-10 as assumed and confirm it with the user, or drop it.

findings.text: REQ-10 does not say which state a rescheduled Stale appointment takes (Scheduled again?), so a tester cannot check the result.

cites.quote: title: Staff can reschedule a Stale appointment

findings.suggested_fix: State the resulting state, for example 'becomes Scheduled with the new start time'.

findings.text: The summary says this is the product's first background job, but no claim or cite backs it. The only evidence is the architecture#open-points reference inside the A-01 question.

cites.quote: this is the product's first background job
The system has no background jobs yet (architecture#open-points)

findings.suggested_fix: Add a claim citing the architecture open-points section.

findings.text: REQ-14 is a task for the glossary owner, not a system behaviour a tester can check, and it overlaps the Out of scope line on editing the glossary.

cites.quote: The glossary owner adds an entry for `Stale` defined as in REQ-2.

findings.suggested_fix: Record the glossary entry as a follow-up action, not as a REQ.

findings.text: REQ-2 states the window twice: '24h after its start time' and the quoted 'within one day'. This is redundant and could be read as two windows.

cites.quote: not marked Completed or rescheduled `within one day`, is marked Stale.
closed by staff once its start time has passed

questions.text: A-03 said staff can still 'close' a Stale appointment. Can staff also reschedule (move) one, and if so, does it go back to Scheduled?
